To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) psychiatric disorders are partly caused by a general genetic risk factor; and (2) this risk factor also influences convictions of violent crimes.

(i) psychiatric disorders and convictions of violence are influenced by a general genetic etiology; (ii) this etiology accounts for 10–36% of the variation in these conditions; and (iii) the general genetic etiology is partly explained by a general genetic liability to psychopathology.
a general genetic influence on psychiatric disorders emerges from a multivariate analysis of the Swedish population, based on a national register of psychiatric diagnoses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic and environmental etiology of psychiatric disorders.
the etiological factors of mental disorders and the extent to which they overlap.
genetic and environmental factors in the development of common psychiatric disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a general genetic component influences all psychiatric disorders and violent crimes.
a general factor of psychopathologies, including both mental disorders and criminal behavior, is influenced by genetic factors.
the majority of psychiatric disorders have a common genetic etiology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a general genetic risk factor influences the liability to develop a variety of psychiatric problems.

there is a general factor of genetic liability to psychopathology that is shared across multiple disorders, which is consistent with previous research and with the idea that psychiatric disorders are not discrete entities but instead are part of a continuum.
there is a general genetic factor influencing a wide range of psychiatric disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a set of genes influences a variety of psychiatric conditions, and that this genetic factor is shared across the entire spectrum of psychopathology.
the genetic overlap between disorders is not a methodological artifact, but a robust finding across different ascertainment strategies.
the general factor of psychopathological liability is not an artifact of the sampling procedure.
